titulo: Playwright MCP in Claude Code/Codex: the accessibility snapshot in practice
lead: Playwright MCP gives your coding agent a browser. It doesn't send a screenshot: it sends the accessibility snapshot, with a reference (ref) on each control, and the agent acts through those refs. In this lesson a script makes exactly the calls the agent would make, without a model, and then you connect the server to Claude Code or Codex.
objetivo: do with Playwright MCP what the agent does: read the snapshot, find the control by its ref and act, and connect the server to your agent.

aprende.t: The snapshot with refs (e13, e15, e18)
The calls: navigate, snapshot, type, select, click, wait_for
The common mistake: taking the snapshot before the page has finished loading
Connect to Claude Code (.mcp.json) and Codex (config.toml)

hero_alt: A laptop open in a dark terminal, next to a monitor showing a booking form, neutral office light.

nos.detalhe: The agent opens the URL. Playwright MCP 0.0.83 replies with the URL, the title, how many errors are in the console and, if the page registered WebMCP tools, how many there are (lesson 4).
browser_snapshot returns the accessibility tree in YAML: role, name and one ref per element, like textbox "Seu nome" [ref=e13]. It's the same format course 0 printed, now with refs.
The model reads the snapshot and picks the ref. In the dry run, ver-como-agente.mjs does the picking, looking for role and name. If a control has no name, neither one can find it reliably.
browser_type, browser_select_option and browser_click receive target (the ref) and element (a text description, used to ask for permission). Then a new snapshot shows the result.

secoes.legenda: A ref is valid for that snapshot only. If the page changed, take another.

secoes.titulo: What the agent receives and what it does

texto: The server exposes 25 browser tools (browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_type, browser_select_option, browser_wait_for, browser_console_messages…). The agent sees them all in the list and chooses.
The project's documentation today also recommends a CLI-and-skills route for coding agents; the kit uses the tools over MCP, which is what Claude Code and Codex read.
In the dry run, the script found textbox "Seu nome" = e13, combobox "Serviço" = e15 and button "Ver horários" = e18 and acted through them. No pixels.
That's why the HTML from course 0 matters: the label becomes the name, and the name is how the agent finds the ref.

The times arrive 1.5 s after the click. With browser_wait_for waiting for the text "horários livres para", the snapshot comes back complete. Without waiting, you get "Carregando horários…" and zero times.
Wait for the text that proves the result, not for a number of seconds.

exemplo.texto: An agent that takes the snapshot too early answers "there are no times" with full confidence. Lesson 7 comes back to this case.

secoes.titulo: The dry run: the agent's calls, without a model
secoes.sub: ver-como-agente.mjs connects Playwright MCP over stdio, the way Claude Code would, and does the task "see the times for Revisão completa".

blocos.rot: Terminal · do the task through Playwright MCP
Terminal · the same, without waiting for the list

abas.html:
→ browser_navigate {"url":"http://127.0.0.1:PORTA/agendar.html"}
→ browser_snapshot {}
  achei: textbox "Seu nome" = e13 · combobox "Serviço" = e15 · button "Ver horários" = e18
→ browser_type {"target":"e13","text":"Ana"}
→ browser_select_option {"target":"e15","values":["Revisão completa"]}
→ browser_click {"target":"e18"}
→ browser_wait_for {"text":"horários livres para"}
→ browser_snapshot {}
  status na página: 2 horários livres para Revisão completa em 2026-11-03.
tarefa: horários de Revisão completa em 2026-11-03 → 2 (08:00, 13:00) em 7 chamadas
saída: 0

Seven calls. Each line with → is a tool called by the MCP client; PORTA stands in for the local server's random port.

→ browser_navigate {"url":"http://127.0.0.1:PORTA/agendar.html"}
→ browser_snapshot {}
  achei: textbox "Seu nome" = e13 · combobox "Serviço" = e15 · button "Ver horários" = e18
→ browser_type {"target":"e13","text":"Ana"}
→ browser_select_option {"target":"e15","values":["Revisão completa"]}
→ browser_click {"target":"e18"}
→ browser_snapshot {}
  status na página: Carregando horários…
tarefa: horários de Revisão completa em 2026-11-03 → 0 (nenhum) em 6 chamadas
  a lista ainda estava carregando quando o snapshot foi tirado
saída: 1

Without browser_wait_for, the snapshot catches "Carregando horários…". The script exits with 1, but a hurried agent would say there's no time available.

Here the site is inema.club, INEMA's own. On your machine, swap in the address of one of your own sites: a browser agent only against your own site. The summary shows how many lines and refs the agent receives; inema.club has an origin trial token, so the kit's Chromium 156 also saw its 8 WebMCP tools, with no flag at all.

Chromium do kit: chromium-1248/chrome-linux-arm64/chrome
escrevi kit/pw-config.json e kit/.mcp.json (servidores: playwright, devtools)

# Codex: cole em ~/.codex/config.toml se quiser os mesmos servidores lá
[mcp_servers.playwright]
command = "~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72/kit/node_modules/.bin/playwright-mcp"
args = ["--config", "~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72/kit/pw-config.json"]

[mcp_servers.devtools]
command = "~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72/kit/node_modules/.bin/chrome-devtools-mcp"
args = ["--headless", "--isolated", "--executablePath", "~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1248/chrome-linux-arm64/chrome", "--no-usage-statistics", "--no-performance-crux", "--chromeArg=--no-sandbox"]

playwright:
  Scope: Project config (shared via .mcp.json)
  Status: ⏸ Pending approval (run `claude` to approve)
  Type: stdio
  Command: ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72/kit/node_modules/.bin/playwright-mcp
  Args: --config ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72/kit/pw-config.json

To remove this server, run: claude mcp remove playwright -s project
saída: 0

configurar.mjs writes kit/.mcp.json (Claude Code, project scope) and prints the Codex snippet (in the capture, ~ abbreviates the path; the script prints the absolute path, which is what Codex needs), which you paste into ~/.codex/config.toml if you want. A project server stays "Pending approval" until you open claude inside kit/ and approve it; after that, /mcp shows the server connected (that step was not captured).

perguntas.p: The snapshot shows textbox "Seu nome" [ref=e13]. How does the agent type into this field?
opcoes: It calls browser_type with target e13 and the text
It clicks the field's coordinates on a screenshot
It runs document.getElementById('nome') in the console
It asks the user to copy the text into the field
perguntas.explica: Playwright MCP acts through the snapshot ref. Coordinates are the computer use path; the console is another server (lesson 3).

perguntas.p: The agent clicked "Ver horários", took the snapshot right away, and saw "Carregando horários…". What was missing?
opcoes: A snapshot with a screenshot alongside the tree
Waiting for the text that proves the result
Double-clicking the button to force the list
Reloading the page before clicking the button
perguntas.explica: browser_wait_for with the text "horários livres para" waits for the proof. Reloading loses what was filled in; clicking again fires another search.

perguntas.p: What is the element field for in click and type calls?
opcoes: So the server can find the control when the ref fails
To indicate the ARIA role the control should have
To describe the action in text and ask for permission
So Playwright can generate the control's CSS selector
perguntas.explica: element is the human-readable description used to ask the person for permission; the target (the ref) is what finds the control.

perguntas.p: After configurar.mjs, claude mcp get shows "Pending approval". What should you do?
opcoes: Delete .mcp.json and add the server in the global scope
Run configurar.mjs again with the --webmcp flag
Install stable Chrome, which the server requires
Open claude inside kit/ and approve the server
perguntas.explica: A project server (.mcp.json) needs approval the first time. The kit uses Playwright's Chromium; it doesn't need stable Chrome.

itens.texto: The agent receives the accessibility tree and acts through refs, not pixels.
A snapshot taken too early becomes a wrong answer that looks right.
A .mcp.json in the kit for Claude Code, the same snippet in Codex's config.toml.
